functional.title: Verify API documentation page is accessible and loads correctly
preconditions: User is logged into the application with a valid account
API documentation has been published and deployed
User has permissions to view documentation resources
Browser is a modern supported browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)

steps.action: Navigate to the API documentation URL (e.g., /docs/api or /api-reference)
steps.expectedResult: API documentation page loads successfully with HTTP 200 status code

steps.action: Verify the page header and title display correctly
steps.expectedResult: Page displays the title 'API Documentation' or equivalent, with proper branding and navigation elements

steps.action: Check that the table of contents or navigation sidebar is present
steps.expectedResult: A structured navigation panel is visible listing all API endpoints grouped by resource/category

steps.action: Verify that at least one API endpoint entry displays method, path, and description
steps.expectedResult: Each endpoint shows HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), endpoint path, and a brief description of its purpose

steps.action: Check that the page loads within acceptable time (under 5 seconds)
steps.expectedResult: Full page content including all sections renders within 5 seconds on standard broadband connection

postconditions: API documentation page remains accessible and stable
User can continue navigating to other sections of the documentation
No console errors or broken resource links are present

functional.title: Verify API endpoint details display request parameters and response schemas
preconditions: User is on the API documentation page
At least one API endpoint is documented with full details
Documentation includes request/response schema definitions

steps.action: Click on a specific API endpoint entry (e.g., 'GET /api/v1/users')
steps.expectedResult: Endpoint detail section expands or navigates to show full documentation for that endpoint

steps.action: Verify the request parameters section is displayed
steps.expectedResult: Request parameters table shows parameter name, type, required/optional flag, and description for each parameter

steps.action: Verify the request body schema is displayed (for POST/PUT endpoints)
steps.expectedResult: Request body section shows JSON schema with field names, data types, constraints, and example values

steps.action: Verify the response schema section is displayed
steps.expectedResult: Response section shows expected HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500) with corresponding response body schemas

steps.action: Check that example request and response payloads are provided
steps.expectedResult: Code blocks display properly formatted JSON examples for both request and response bodies

steps.action: Verify that authentication requirements are clearly stated
steps.expectedResult: A section or badge indicates the authentication method required (e.g., 'Bearer Token', 'API Key') for the endpoint

postconditions: All endpoint details are fully visible and correctly formatted
User can copy example payloads from the documentation
Navigation back to the endpoint list is available

functional.title: Verify user guide is accessible and contains structured content sections

steps.action: Verify the table of contents lists all major sections
steps.expectedResult: Table of contents displays sections such as 'Getting Started', 'Installation', 'Configuration', 'Features', 'Troubleshooting', and 'FAQ'

steps.action: Click on the 'Getting Started' section link in the table of contents
steps.expectedResult: Page scrolls to or navigates to the Getting Started section with introductory content, prerequisites, and first steps

steps.action: Verify that the Getting Started section contains step-by-step instructions
steps.expectedResult: Section displays numbered or ordered steps with clear instructions, screenshots or diagrams where applicable

steps.action: Navigate back to the table of contents and click on another section (e.g., 'Features')
steps.expectedResult: Page navigates to the Features section displaying feature descriptions with usage instructions

postconditions: User guide remains accessible throughout the session
All internal navigation links within the guide function correctly

edgeCases.title: API documentation handles simultaneous edits by multiple users on the same endpoint
preconditions: Two separate user accounts (User A and User B) both have documentation editor permissions
Both users are logged in on separate browser sessions

steps.action: User A opens the edit form for 'GET /api/v1/users' endpoint documentation
steps.expectedResult: Edit form loads with current description 'Original description' for User A

steps.action: User B simultaneously opens the same edit form for 'GET /api/v1/users' endpoint documentation

steps.action: User A changes description to 'Updated by User A' and clicks 'Save'
steps.expectedResult: User A's changes save successfully with confirmation message

steps.action: User B (still seeing 'Original description') changes description to 'Updated by User B' and clicks 'Save'
steps.expectedResult: System either: (a) shows conflict warning 'This document was modified by another user. Please review changes before saving', or (b) saves User B's version with version history preserved, or (c) rejects save with error message about stale data

steps.expectedResult: Description shows a consistent state - either User A's or User B's version, not a corrupted merge

steps.action: Check version history or audit log for the endpoint
steps.expectedResult: Both edit attempts are logged; version history shows the sequence of changes with timestamps and user attribution

postconditions: No data corruption occurred from concurrent edits
Version history accurately reflects all edit attempts
Final state of documentation is consistent and readable
Audit trail shows both users' actions with timestamps

edgeCases.title: Documentation system handles browser back/forward navigation without losing unsaved changes
preconditions: User is logged in with documentation editor permissions
User guide editor is open with an existing section loaded
Browser history has at least one previous page entry
No auto-save is configured or auto-save interval is longer than test duration

steps.action: Open user guide section editor and make changes to the content (add paragraph 'Unsaved changes test')
steps.expectedResult: Content is modified in the editor; no save has been triggered

steps.action: Click the browser's Back button without saving
steps.expectedResult: Browser shows a confirmation dialog: 'You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave this page?' or equivalent beforeunload warning

steps.action: Click 'Stay on page' or 'Cancel' in the confirmation dialog
steps.expectedResult: User remains on the editor page; all unsaved changes are preserved in the editor

steps.action: Click the browser's Back button again and this time confirm leaving the page
steps.expectedResult: Browser navigates to the previous page; unsaved changes are lost as expected

steps.action: Click the browser's Forward button to return to the editor
steps.expectedResult: Editor page loads; content shows the last saved version (without the unsaved paragraph); editor is in a clean state

steps.action: Verify no partial or corrupted data was saved during the navigation
steps.expectedResult: Published documentation shows only the last explicitly saved version; no ghost content appears

postconditions: Unsaved changes are properly discarded when user confirms navigation away
No partial saves or data corruption occurred
Editor loads cleanly when navigated back to via browser history
Published documentation remains in its last explicitly saved state
